verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Daman until plant-level regulatory status is clean; lend only to niche, compliant API/CDMO units with tight structure.
title: Daman Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Daman pharma unit buys solvents, intermediates and API inputs, runs them through reactors and finishing lines, and sells into formulations players or export markets.** Cash is made on yield and quality consistency, not on price — a single failed audit can freeze a customer's order book overnight. Value sits in the approved-vendor status and the regulatory file, not the building. **So when a proposal lands, check which plants hold current, valid approvals and for which market; if the customer cannot name the last audit date and outcome, ask for the certificate and the Form 483 history.**

## Where cash actually sits
**Working capital is the business: long receivables and high inventory holding are structural, with working capital intensity running at 47-52% in the peer set [10].** Capex is heavy and lumpy, and term debt is often back-ended — one rated peer carried Rs 152 crore of term loans with repayments starting only from May 2025 [9]. Pricing power is thin for plain API and strong only for niche or CDMO work. **So size the drawing power on actual receivables ageing, not on the sales projection; if inventory days exceed the peer range, ask for the stock statement and slow-moving list.**

## What has changed now
**The local signal is regulatory, not commercial: Alkem's Daman facility drew seven USFDA observations after a 12-day inspection from April 20 to May 1, 2026 [2][3], even though the same site had Malta GMP clearance from a December 2025 inspection, valid three years [3].** That combination tells you a site can be EU-clean and US-flagged at once — approvals are market-specific. Nationally, IIP for NIC 21 is +1.6% YoY [D] while overall output is -2.1% [D] and bank credit is +21.6% YoY [D], a +23.7 pp gap [D]: money is chasing this sector faster than output. **So treat any Daman pharma proposal with recent credit growth and flat sales as a warning, and ask why the borrowing is outrunning the topline.**

## Where to grow, and how
**Pursue niche API and CDMO units, not commodity formulators.** Peers show the spread: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of Rs 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth with an acquisition planned within 12 months [5]. **So favour borrowers with a named molecule, a contracted customer and CDMO-style sticky orders; avoid single-customer, single-market units — one rated peer's revenue fell on weak US contract-research demand before recovering 35% in 7M FY2025 [8].** Structure with a receivables-backed drawing power, monthly stock and book-debt statements, and a covenant capping total debt to a level you set from the customer's own cash flows — collect from customer.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the audit calendar first: any new Form 483, import alert or repeat observation at the borrower's plant is an immediate stop.** Then watch receivable days and inventory build against the 47-52% intensity benchmark [10], and limit utilisation drifting up without sales growth. **If a borrower's export billing shifts to a single destination or a single buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for the customer contract and payment history before renewing.**
watch: New Form 483 or import alert at borrower plant -> freeze new limits, review existing drawing power
Inventory days or receivable days rise beyond agreed band -> cut drawing power, seek ageing detail
Utilisation rises while invoiced sales are flat -> ask for order book and customer-wise billing
Single buyer crosses one-third of sales -> obtain contract and payment record before renewal
Back-ended repayments approaching without cash build -> restructure to tighter amortisation
